The scores across all three paths are consistent, with a final score of 0.7172, suggesting a strong level of confidence in the observed relationships. The mechanism appears to involve a common pathway where the virus antigen interacts with a shared target compound, magnesium levulinate, which then influences the protein disulfide-isomerase. The evidence is robust and consistent, but it does not exclude the possibility of alternative pathways or additional factors influencing the relationship.
